title: 2015 Roseville Legal Studies Trial
notes: The paper has no answer key; an exact-paper search found the exam listing but no separate answers. Answers are reasoned guesses. Questions 12–13 share a scenario. The MC pages contain no figures needed to answer questions.

groups.stimulus: Peter, 15, has been detained by the police on suspicion of being involved in a series of vandalism offences in the local area.

questions.stem: What is the legal term for the mental element of a crime?

options.D: Causation

questions.answerNote: Mens rea is the legal term for the mental element of an offence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a public order offence?

options.D: Stealing $100 worth of cosmetics

questions.answerNote: Swearing in public is the public order offence among these options.

questions.stem: Danielle is being tried for importing illegal drugs into Australia. She claims she was compelled to commit the crime. Which of the following defences is she relying on?

options.D: Duress

questions.answerNote: Duress applies where threats compel a person to commit an offence.

questions.stem: The right to life is best protected under which human rights instrument?

options.B: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
options.D: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights

questions.answerNote: ICCPR Art 6 is the binding instrument protecting the right to life; B (UDHR Art 3) is the other plausible answer but the UDHR is not binding.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of the role of witnesses in a criminal trial?

options.A: They must have actually seen the offence.
options.B: They can give evidence through oral testimony.
options.C: They can tell the court what they heard about an offence.
options.D: They can be questioned by the victim and the victim’s barrister.

questions.answerNote: Witnesses can give evidence orally; The other choices impose incorrect limits or identify the wrong examiner.

questions.stem: What is the role of the jury in a criminal trial?

options.A: To provide reasons for their decision in the case
options.B: To decide on an appropriate sentence for the accused
options.C: To find the evidence to determine the verdict of the case
options.D: To listen to the evidence and then hand down their verdict

questions.answerNote: A jury hears the evidence and determines the verdict.

questions.stem: In sentencing a convicted offender, Justice Davis must hand down a sentence of at least 5 years imprisonment. Which of the following will most affect the judge’s sentencing decision?

options.D: Judicial guidelines

questions.answerNote: A statutory minimum constrains the available sentence through legislation.

questions.stem: The right of all peoples to live free from conflict is an example of which of the following?

options.D: Peace rights

questions.answerNote: Freedom from conflict is a collective peace right.

questions.stem: Shaun is nineteen and has been charged with a serious indictable offence. This charge will first be heard in which court?

options.D: Children’s Court

questions.answerNote: Serious indictable matters begin with committal proceedings in the Local Court.

questions.stem: In sentencing an offender, the judge states that the offender “is remorseful and understands the consequences of her actions”. What has the judge considered in this sentencing decision?

options.D: Charge negotiation

questions.answerNote: Remorse is a mitigating factor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true about human rights?

options.A: Violations occur daily across the globe
options.B: They are universal, inalienable, inherent and indivisible
options.C: They enable people to achieve their full potential in society
options.D: They are enforced by the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

questions.answerNote: The UDHR is a declaration and does not itself enforce rights.

questions.stem: In the event that Peter’s matter goes to court, the burden of proving Peter’s guilt will fall on which of the following?

options.D: The local people

questions.answerNote: The prosecution bears the burden in criminal proceedings.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true for Peter?

options.A: He cannot be charged for at least 4 hours.
options.B: One of his parents can be present when he is questioned.
options.C: If he is charged, the matter will be heard in the Local Court.
options.D: He can be questioned for as long as necessary to find the truth.

questions.answerNote: A parent or responsible adult may be present during police questioning of a young person.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the criminal investigation process?

options.D: Collection of DNA from the crime scene

questions.answerNote: Charge negotiation occurs within case processing/prosecution rather than criminal investigation.

questions.stem: In relation to human rights, the media is most effective at which of the following?

options.D: Incorporation

questions.answerNote: Media reporting raises awareness and promotes human rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the most effective legal measure the Australian government could use to deal with transnational crimes?

options.A: Appearing before the International Criminal Court
options.B: Boycotting the United Nations General Assembly
options.C: Entering into cooperative arrangements with other nation states
options.D: Publicising crimes with the aim of deterring future offenders

questions.answerNote: Transnational crime requires legal cooperation between affected states.

questions.stem: In what way does a victim impact statement help to promote justice?

options.A: It provides the victim with a voice during the sentencing process.
options.B: It allows the victim to present transcript evidence during the trial.
options.C: It gives the victim some input into the charge negotiation process.
options.D: It allows the victim to have a say regarding the collection of evidence.

questions.answerNote: A victim impact statement gives the victim’s account of harm to the sentencing court.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines doli incapax?

options.A: The preferential treatment of a child in the Children’s Court
options.B: The rebuttable presumption of incapacity for 10–14 year olds
options.C: The presumption that a child is incapable of committing a crime
options.D: The absence of a committal hearing for a child under 15 years of age

questions.answerNote: Doli incapax is the rebuttable presumption that a child aged 10–14 lacks criminal capacity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an argument against Australia adopting a Charter of Rights?

options.B: The marginalised and disadvantaged won’t be supported
options.C: Human rights are already adequately protected in Australia
options.D: It will inhibit the building of a culture of respect for human rights

questions.answerNote: Opponents argue that existing protections make a statutory charter unnecessary.

questions.stem: While committing an armed robbery, Emily accidently fires her weapon and injures a worker. She co-operates with police and pleads guilty to the offence. Which of the following is true regarding Emily?

options.A: She will appear before a jury.
options.C: Her case will be finalised in the Local Court.
options.D: She can use the defence of mistake during her trial.

questions.answerNote: A guilty plea removes the need for a contested trial, so Emily would not be cross-examined as an accused giving evidence.
